title: John Glasgow in Quothquan: testament dative, 1685
record: National Records of Scotland, Lanark Commissary Court, CC14/5/12, images 67-68
coverage: Both supplied original images were rendered at 300 DPI, visually inspected in full and re-read in enlarged overlapping bands. This is a full line-oriented working transcription of John Glasgow's entry, not a diplomatic edition. Image 67 has dense show-through and darkened strokes; image 68 has a repaired/dark left strip. The following Morgan testament beginning low on image 68 is outside John's entry and excluded. Brackets preserve uncertain readings; routine legal clauses are transcribed line by line but not completed from boilerplate where the ink is unreadable.

plain_english: John Glasgow lived at Quothquan in Libberton parish, within the presbytery of Lanark. He died intestate in February 1685.

Jonet, whose surname may read Kinnie but remains paleographically uncertain, is explicitly called John's relict and executrix dative. Relict means widow; executrix dative is the court-appointed estate role.

The proceeding is dated 25 March 1685. The inventory includes livestock, crops or fodder, household/farm goods and the deceased's clothing, but the dense show-through prevents a dependable item-by-item valuation.
William Wilkie acts as procurator fiscal in the court language. That is an official/procedural role, not evidence of kinship.
William Watson is the cautioner who guarantees that the estate goods will be made available to interested parties. Cautioner is a security role and does not make him a relative.
The supplied testament names no child and no parent. It does not bridge this Quothquan man to the 1608 Mid Calder baptism.
findings: Direct identity: John Glasgow in Quothquan, Libberton parish, presbytery of Lanark.
Direct death evidence: intestate, died in February 1685; court proceeding dated 25 March 1685.
Direct spouse role: Jonet is called relict. Her surname resembles Kinnie in the opening and continuation but is not clear enough for an unqualified surname.
Direct administration: Jonet is executrix dative; William Wilkie is procurator fiscal; William Watson is cautioner. None of those offices supplies an unstated biological relationship.
No child or parent is named in the supplied entry. Existing father or child attachments cannot be upgraded from this testament.
The next testament begins on image 68 and is a separate record; its names and facts must not be merged into John's estate.
changes_from_previous: Fresh inspection of both originals preceded comparison with research/Glasgow-1086/findings.md and the relationship index.
The earlier Quothquan, Libberton, February 1685, relict and executrix readings are supported directly by the manuscript.
The widow's surname is less secure than a plain 'Kinnie': heavy show-through and compressed letter joins leave Kinnie as a qualified reading only.
The re-read keeps William Wilkie's procurator-fiscal role and William Watson's cautioner role separate from family evidence.
No line in the supplied testament names a child or parent, so the Mid Calder baptism and attached descendants remain external, uncertain identifications.

confidence_statement: High for John Glasgow's Quothquan/Libberton identity, February 1685 death, Jonet as relict and executrix dative, and the 25 March proceeding. High that William Wilkie and William Watson hold administrative rather than stated kin roles, and high that no child or parent is named. Moderate-low for Jonet's surname and many inventory/debt details because of severe show-through, dark strokes and a repaired page edge. This is a complete working reading of the supplied entry, not a silent reconstruction of obscured boilerplate.
